classification.difficultyReason: Use the established leg ratio and Pythagoras to prove both remaining corresponding-side ratios.

content.prompt: The two right-triangles below have equal angles. In Theorem 1 we proved that $\frac oa=\frac OA$. Using this fact, additionally prove that $\frac oh=\frac OH$ and $\frac ah=\frac AH$.

spec.description: Smaller triangle at left, horizontal base a, vertical right leg o and hypotenuse h. Decorative cyan fill omitted.
spec.mathematics: Theta bottom left and right angle bottom right.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied symbolic labels remain visible.

spec.description: Larger corresponding triangle at right, horizontal base A, vertical right leg O and hypotenuse H. Decorative orange fill omitted.
spec.mathematics: Theta bottom left and right angle bottom right; same shape as the smaller triangle.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied symbolic labels remain visible.

answer.short:
$\frac oh=\frac OH$ and $\frac ah=\frac AH$.

Use $A=\frac{aO}{o}$ and Pythagoras to obtain $H=\frac{Oh}{o}$, then divide.
answer.worked:
The given equality gives $A=\frac{aO}{o}$, with all side lengths positive. By Pythagoras, $h^2=a^2+o^2$ and
$$\begin{align*}H&=\sqrt{A^2+O^2}\\H&=\sqrt{\left(\frac{aO}{o}\right)^2+O^2}\\H&=O\sqrt{\frac{a^2+o^2}{o^2}}\\H&=\frac{Oh}{o}.\end{align*}$$
Therefore,
$$\begin{align*}\frac OH&=\frac O{Oh/o}\\\frac OH&=\frac oh,\\\frac AH&=\frac{aO/o}{Oh/o}\\\frac AH&=\frac ah.\end{align*}$$
